Order No.12 / Dated : 15.04.2024 1.

Order rejecting anticipatory bail of the appellant in connection with Lohardaga SC/ST P.S. Case No.06/2023 registered under Sections 376 and 379 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 3 and 4 of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act (in short 'SC/ST Act'), is under challenge in the instant criminal appeal.

entities.text: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. Complaint filed by Surajmuni Oraon on 08.09.2022 is the basis of the case which was forwarded under Section 156(3) of the Cr.P.C. for registration as FIR.

The case of the complainant/informant as disclosed in the complaint petition is that scooty bearing registration no.JH01BC 4060 of the complainant was forcibly taken by the appellant/accused in June, 2022 and he came to the complainant and asked her that if you want to take back your scooty, you have to come to my residence.
When she went to his house to get her scooty back, it is alleged that rape was committed with her and repeated on different occasion.
Later on, when she informed about the incidence to her husband, she was advised to lodge a criminal case.
3. It is submitted by the learned counsel on behalf of appellant the complainant is a married major lady and in the entire complaint, date and time of the alleged incidence has not been disclosed.

As a matter of fact, this is counter to Complaint Case No.577 of 2019 which had been filed by Ashraf Ansari against the complainant under Section 138 of the N.I. Act who had taken friendly loan of Rs.1,49,000/- and in order to pressurize the appellant, absolutely false case has been filed against him.
After the warrant of arrest was issued in that case under Section 138 of the N.I. Act, the present case was filed.

It is also submitted that complaint also does not disclose as to why the offence under SC/ST Act will be made as there is no reference to casteist remark having been made within the Ashraf Ansari vs The State Of Jharkhand on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62318719/
1 public view.

entities.text: Ashraf Ansari vs The State Of Jharkhand
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Prosecution is not sustainable in view of the judgment rendered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Hitesh Verma Versus State of Uttrakhand & Another, (2020) 10 SCC 71, no case under SC/ST Act will not be made out.

entities.text: Hitesh Verma Versus State of Uttrakhand & Another, (2020) 10 SCC 71
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. Learned A.P.P. assisted by learned counsel on behalf of informant have vehemently opposed the prayer.

It is submitted that the appellant is named in the FIR and there is direct and specific allegation of committing repeated sexual assault on the complainant and also abusing her by calling her caste name.
It is also submitted that the anticipatory bail application is barred under Section 18(2) of the SC/ST Act.
Prosecution case has been supported by one of the witness in the case diary namely Sumesh Bhagat.

5. Having considered the submission advanced on behalf of both sides, it is apparent that the complainant was on litigating term with the appellant who had filed a case under Section 138 of the N.I. Act against her.
The complainant is a major married lady and the complaint petition is absolutely silent about the date, time and place of the offence.
6. Considering the submissions made, the anticipatory bail application is allowed.

Accordingly, the appellant, above named, is directed to surrender before the learned trial Court within a period of four weeks and in the event of his arrest or surrender, he shall be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand only) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the court of learned Additional Sessions Judge-1 cum Special Judge SC/ST (POA), Lohardaga, in connection with Lohardaga P.S. Case No. 06 of 2023 subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure and he appellant will co
- operate with the investigation and will appear under Section 41A Cr.P.C. as and when required and comply.

7. Accordingly, this Criminal Appeal is allowed and the impugned order dated 26.05.2023 passed in Anticipatory Bail Petition No. 134 of 2023 by learned Additional Sessions Judge-1 cum Special Judge SC/ST (POA), Lohardaga in connection with Lohardaga P.S. Case No. 06 of 2023, is set- aside.
